name: Pyrrhus
overview: Pyrrhus is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament, noted primarily as the possible father of Sopater. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal details recorded about him in Scripture. His mention is brief and serves to identify his son within the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: The name Pyrrhus appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Acts 20:4. There is no provided meaning or divine attribution for this proper name, and no additional titles are recorded.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Pyrrhus is the father of Sopater, as indicated in Acts 20:4. Beyond this paternal connection, no other family relationships are documented or elaborated upon in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pyrrhus is significant primarily as the father of Sopater, who is mentioned among the companions of Paul during his missionary journeys. This connection situates Pyrrhus within the network of early believers who supported the spread of the gospel. Although Pyrrhus himself is not directly active in the narrative, his identification helps to trace the lineage and community of early Christians.
